title: Unified Terahertz Framework for Magnetic and Lattice Responses Reveals an Elusive Ordering Transition in Gd$_2$Ru$_2$O$_7$
authors: Nicolas M. Kawahala, Rafael L. Sabainsk, Esteban Marulanda, Rafael S. Freitas, Felix G. G. Hernandez
abstract: Magnetic order in materials combining localized rare-earth moments with itinerant transition-metal sublattices generates internal fields whose lattice imprint is rarely accessed directly. In Gd pyrochlore ruthenate, we find that a single terahertz spectrum resolves an exchange-split Gd$^{3+}$ mode and an optical phonon. Their coupled evolution quantifies the internal field, oriented as predicted for cluster-multipolar order, and reveals a Gd-ordering transition elusive to bulk thermodynamic probes, establishing a unified framework for accessing magnetic and lattice responses in correlated quantum materials.
summary: This work uses THz spectroscopy on $	ext{Gd}_2	ext{Ru}_2	ext{O}_7$ to simultaneously measure magnetic and lattice responses. By modeling the coupled evolution of these two spectral features, the authors successfully quantify an internal magnetic field and reveal a subtle Gd-ordering transition previously hidden from bulk measurements.
main_problem: The study aims to understand how magnetic order couples to lattice vibrations (spin-lattice coupling) in $	ext{Gd}_2	ext{Ru}_2	ext{O}_7$ and reveal an ordering transition that is difficult to detect using standard bulk thermodynamic measurements.
main_result: By simultaneously measuring magnetic excitations and optical phonons via THz spectroscopy, the authors quantified an internal exchange field ($B_{	ext{int}}$) consistent with cluster-multipolar order and provided independent spectroscopic evidence for a low-temperature Gd-ordering transition.
method:
Magneto-Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy (THz-TDS) was employed to measure the complex optical conductivity ($\sigma(
u)$) across both magnetic and phonon frequency ranges as a function of temperature and external magnetic field.
model_or_system: The physical system is the pyrochlore ruthenate $	ext{Gd}_2	ext{Ru}_2	ext{O}_7$, which contains localized $4f$ moments ($	ext{Gd}^{3+}$) coupled to itinerant $	ext{Ru}$ magnetism. The analysis models spectral features using uncoupled Lorentz oscillators superimposed on a quadratic background.
key_observables:
Low-frequency magnetic resonance parameters ($\Omega_m, 
u_m, 	au_m$), optical phonon parameters ($\Omega_p, 
u_p, 	au_p$), and the integrated spectral weights ($W_m, W_p$).
important_parameters: Temperatures ranging from $1.6	ext{ K}$ to $200	ext{ K}$, external magnetic fields up to $7	ext{ T}$, and derived internal exchange field values ($\approx 5-6 	ext{ T}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the spectral response in each region can be modeled by an uncoupled Lorentz oscillator on a smooth quadratic background, allowing for independent fitting of magnetic and phonon components.
figures_summary:
Figures illustrate the temperature and field dependence of resonance parameters ($\Omega, 
u, 	au$) for both magnetic and phonon modes, showing correlated anomalies at characteristic ordering temperatures. Integrated spectral weights ($W_m, W_p$) are plotted as functions of T and B.
paper_structure: The paper establishes a unified framework by analyzing the temperature and field dependence of two distinct spectroscopic signals—the low-frequency magnetic resonance and the optical phonon mode—to correlate them with known magnetic transition points in $	ext{Gd}_2	ext{Ru}_2	ext{O}_7$.
why_interesting: The technique provides a powerful, non-invasive way to probe coupled quantum phenomena (spin-lattice coupling) by separating and analyzing distinct energy scales within a single spectroscopic measurement.
